approval_evidence.quote: New Drug Application (NDA): 021395 Company: BOEHRINGER INGELHEIM ... SPIRIVA TIOTROPIUM ... Original Approvals or Tentative Approvals ... 01/30/2004 ORIG-1 Approval Type 1 - New Molecular Entity STANDARD

launch_evidence.quote: 2002: Launch of Spiriva® The COPD product Spiriva® is launched.

annual_basis: Calendar years 2012-2024 from the Human Pharma net-sales-by-product table of Boehringer Ingelheim's annual report for each year (EUR million, worldwide); 2012 is the prior-year column of the 2013 report. Years before 2012 are not continuous at any fetchable source, so the series does not start at the 2002 launch and stays context rather than a peak benchmark.
series_start_reason: The 2013 annual report is the earliest full annual report readable at source; it prints Spiriva for 2013 (3,552) and 2012 (3,562). The 2010, 2011 and 2012 reports are not hosted at annualreports.com (404) and boehringer-ingelheim.com serves a bot challenge; 2009 (EUR 2.4 billion, rounded, in the 2009 results press release) is known but 2010-2011 are not, so 2009 is not joined to the series.
series_end_reason: 2024 is the latest annual report readable at source; the 2025 annual report (published in 2026) is not hosted at annualreports.com and the issuer site blocks plain requests.
notes: Boehringer Ingelheim is privately held and reports half-year and full-year results only; Spiriva is printed as a full-year figure in the annual reports, so no quarterly series is possible. The line is the Spiriva brand total (HandiHaler and Respimat). Each year is read from its own report; later reports' prior-year columns agree except 2017 (own report 2,826; 2018 report restates 2,828; own-year used). This series replaces the earlier gold rows (2009 and 2018 rounded to EUR 0.1 billion from press releases, 2021-2023 from annualreport.boehringer-ingelheim.com) with exact figures for a gap-free 2012-2024 run; the old 2021-2023 values are identical. Pfizer, the U.S. co-promoter until early 2014, never printed a Spiriva figure: its releases and Forms 10-K/10-Q include Spiriva only inside the aggregated 'Alliance revenues' line. Source PDFs are Boehringer Ingelheim's own annual reports as archived at annualreports.com, because the issuer's own host refuses scripted requests. Years without a citable copy on Boehringer's own site cite annualreports.com's archived copy of the same annual report, because boehringer-ingelheim.com blocks automated downloads.

no_quarterly_series.source_quote: (c) Includes Enbrel (in the U.S. and Canada), Spiriva, Rebif, Aricept and Eliquis.
no_quarterly_series.details: Boehringer Ingelheim files nothing with the SEC and publishes product sales only for full years (annual report) and, for some products, half-years. The only quarterly reporter, Pfizer (U.S. and selected-country co-promoter, collaboration expiring 2012-2016), prints Spiriva only inside its aggregated Alliance revenues line in every quarterly release 2004-2015 (e.g. 'ALLIANCE REVENUE (Aricept, Mirapex, Rebif and Spiriva) 245' in the Q4 2004 release, and footnote (c) above in the Q2 2013 release). No quarterly Spiriva figure exists; none is interpolated.

search_log: Pfizer (CIK 0000078003): fetched all 70 EX-99 exhibits of 8-K Item 2.02 filings 2004-10 to 2021-02 and grepped 'Spiriva': every table hit is the Alliance revenues aggregate row or its footnote; Q&A prose ('How is Spiriva performing?') carries no figure. Pfizer Forms 10-K 2011 and 2013 and 10-Q Q2 2013 grepped: Spiriva only in co-promotion prose and the Alliance revenues footnote; the 10-Q Q2 2013 states a combined Spiriva/Aricept alliance revenue decline (~$210 million), not a Spiriva figure.
Earlier years: the 2009 results press release prints 'EUR 2.4 billion' (rounded); the 2010-2012 annual reports surfaced only on yumpu.com (not an issuer host) and were not used.
Half-year: BI half-year releases print only top products for six months; a half-year cannot be split into quarters, so they were not pursued for values.
Bigdata.com not used for values; every figure read from the cited PDF.
